speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Restoring Our Covenant with God
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen emphasizes the importance of repairing the spiritual breaches that develop between God and His people throughout history. He highlights the recurring need for covenant renewal among the Israelites as they strayed from God's commands, drawing parallels to contemporary Christians who may also neglect their covenant with God. The key takeaway is that believers must actively seek to restore their relationship with God by adhering to His laws and teachings, thus becoming 'repairers of the breach.'

title: Study In Hebrews Chapter 13
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Call to Brotherly Love in Hebrews 13
summary: In this sermon on Hebrews 13, Mark Bullen emphasizes the importance of brotherly love within the church and the necessity of aligning with God's principles for genuine fellowship. He argues that true reconciliation with God involves embracing His laws and purposes, which in turn fosters authentic relationships among believers. The takeaway is that brotherly love is conditional upon shared values and mutual growth in faith, and that genuine love requires accountability and adherence to biblical truth.

title: Study In Hebrews Chapter 12:11-29
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Enduring Correction: The Path to Righteousness
summary: In this sermon on Hebrews 12:11-29, Mark Bullen emphasizes the importance of enduring God's correction as a sign of true discipleship and love for His law. He argues that suffering is a necessary part of the Christian journey, leading to spiritual growth and eventual glory. The key takeaway is that believers must strive against sin and embrace God's discipline to prove their commitment to righteousness and their place in His kingdom.

title: Study In Hebrews Chapter 12:1-11
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Running the Race of Faith: Lessons from Hebrews 12
summary: In this sermon on Hebrews 12:1-11, Mark Bullen emphasizes the importance of running the race of faith with endurance, drawing on the examples of biblical figures who faced challenges yet remained faithful. He argues that believers have a superior covenant and are surrounded by a 'cloud of witnesses' who serve as examples of faithfulness. The key takeaway is that each individual must focus on their own race, shedding weights and sins that hinder their progress, and looking to Jesus as the ultimate example of endurance and faithfulness.

title: Study In Hebrews Chapter 11:8-40
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Faithful Living: Lessons from Hebrews 11
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores Hebrews 11:8-40, emphasizing the importance of faith as the primary means of pleasing God. He illustrates how figures like Abraham, Moses, and others exemplified faith through their obedience and endurance despite challenges. The key takeaway is that true faith leads to a longing for a better, godly society and a commitment to live according to God's promises, even when the fulfillment seems distant.

title: Study In Hebrews Chapter 11:1-7
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Understanding Faith: Assurance and Evidence in Hebrews 11
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores Hebrews 11:1-7, emphasizing that true faith is a confident assurance in God's promises and evidence of things not seen. He argues that faith has always been the means of salvation, transcending the Old Testament law and rituals. Bullen highlights the importance of understanding faith not as mere belief but as an active response to God's truth, which is essential for pleasing Him and obtaining righteousness.

title: Study In Hebrews Chapter 10
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Superiority of Christ's Sacrifice
summary: In this sermon on Hebrews chapter 10, Mark Bullen emphasizes the superiority of Christ's sacrifice over the Old Testament sacrifices, explaining that the latter were merely shadows of the true redemption found in Jesus. He argues that true worshippers, who are in covenant with God, should not live with a guilty conscience but rather embrace the assurance of forgiveness through Christ's once-for-all sacrifice. The key takeaway is the importance of maintaining one's covenant relationship with God and the consequences of willful sinning against that covenant.

title: Study In Hebrews Chapter 9
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Superiority of Christ's Priesthood
summary: In this sermon on Hebrews Chapter 9, Mark Bullen emphasizes the significance of Christ as the great high priest in the order of Melchizedek, contrasting the old covenant with the new covenant. He explains how the earthly tabernacle and its sacrifices were mere types pointing to the ultimate sacrifice of Christ, which provides believers direct access to God. The key takeaway is that through Christ's sacrifice, believers can approach God with confidence, experiencing true cleansing and moral transformation.

title: Study In Hebrews Chapter 8
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Eternal High Priest: Transitioning from the Old to the New Covenant
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores Hebrews Chapter 8, emphasizing the transition from the Old Covenant of Levitical priesthood and sacrifices to the New Covenant established by Jesus Christ, the eternal high priest after the order of Melchizedek. He argues that the Old Covenant was a temporary arrangement meant to teach about God's redemption plan, which is fulfilled in Christ, who offers true reconciliation with God. The key takeaway is the importance of understanding one's personal relationship with God through Jesus, independent of earthly religious authorities.

title: Study In Hebrews Chapter 7
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Eternal Priesthood of Melchizedek
summary: The sermon explores the significance of Melchizedek as a priest and king in the context of Abraham's faith and the transition from the Levitical priesthood to the priesthood of Jesus Christ. It emphasizes that Melchizedek represents a higher order of priesthood that is eternal and superior, highlighting the importance of faith combined with action. The key takeaway is that Jesus, as a priest after the order of Melchizedek, offers a better hope and a more direct relationship with God, contrasting with the limitations of the Levitical system.

title: The Testings Of Life
speaker: Jesse Herr
title_alt: Strength Through Testing: Lessons from Scripture
summary: In this sermon, Jesse Herr explores the theme of testing in the lives of biblical figures, particularly focusing on Peter, Abraham, and Moses. He emphasizes that tests are not merely challenges but opportunities for growth and deeper faith. The takeaway is that when faced with trials, believers should remember that stumbling can lead to greater strength and that God's blessings often come after passing significant tests of faith.

title: The Sin Virus
speaker: Nathan Bullen
title_alt: The Spiritual Pandemic: Battling the Sin Virus
summary: In this sermon, Nathan Bullen warns about the dangers of the 'sin virus,' drawing parallels between physical and spiritual health. He emphasizes the importance of maintaining a strong relationship with the Holy Spirit to combat sin and avoid spiritual death. The key takeaway is that believers must actively fight against sin and seek spiritual health, as neglecting this can lead to dire consequences for their spiritual lives.

title: Study In Hebrews Chapter 6
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Growing Beyond the Basics: A Call to Spiritual Maturity
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores Hebrews Chapter 6, emphasizing the importance of spiritual maturity and the dangers of turning away from faith in Christ. He warns against the complacency of believers who remain stagnant in their understanding and practice of faith, urging them to grow beyond elementary teachings. The key takeaway is the necessity of perseverance in faith and the consequences of rejecting Christ after having experienced His grace.

title: Study In Hebrews Chapter 5
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Compassionate High Priest: Understanding Our Role in Christ
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores Hebrews Chapter 5, emphasizing the role of Jesus as the compassionate high priest who understands human suffering and temptation. He argues that Jesus' experiences equip Him to guide and reconcile believers to God, highlighting the importance of sound doctrine and the call for Christians to grow in their faith and understanding. The takeaway is that believers are called to be ambassadors for Christ, representing God accurately and preparing to rule with Him in His kingdom.

title: Study In Hebrews Chapter 4
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Entering God's Rest: A Call to Enduring Faith
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores Hebrews chapter 4, emphasizing the importance of holding fast to faith and the dangers of unbelief as illustrated by the Israelites in the wilderness. He argues that the promise of entering God's rest is conditional upon enduring faith, and warns against the complacency that can lead to spiritual failure. The key takeaway is the urgent call to diligence in faith, ensuring that believers do not fall short of God's promised rest.

title: Study In Hebrews 2:5-3:19
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Supremacy of Christ: Restoring Paradise Lost
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores Hebrews 2:5-3:19, emphasizing the superiority of Christ over angels and His role as the second Adam who restores what was lost through Adam's sin. He argues that Jesus, by becoming flesh, fulfills God's original design for humanity and will ultimately reign over a restored creation. The key takeaway is the importance of holding fast to faith in Christ, who is our high priest and mediator, and the assurance of salvation through Him.

title: Study In Hebrews 1:3-2:4
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Radiating Christ: Understanding His Supremacy
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores Hebrews 1:1-2, emphasizing the supremacy of Christ as the radiance of God's glory and the express image of His person. He argues that Jesus, as the Son of God, is distinct yet of the same essence as the Father, and that believers are called to radiate Christ's character in their lives. The takeaway is the importance of reflecting God's light and character in a world filled with distractions and false expressions of self.

title: Study In Hebrews 1:1-2
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Superiority of Christ: Understanding Hebrews
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores the significance of the book of Hebrews, emphasizing its Jewish context and the superiority of Christ over angels, Moses, and Aaron. He argues that understanding the Jewish roots of Christianity is crucial for grasping the true message of the gospel and warns against the dilution of biblical teachings through later Gentile interpretations. The takeaway is the importance of adhering to the original teachings and understanding of Scripture as intended by the apostles.

title: There Is Grace In Your Place
speaker: Philip Herr
title_alt: Finding Grace in Your God-Given Place
summary: In this sermon, Philip Herr emphasizes the importance of maintaining one's God-given place and responsibilities amidst trials and temptations. He uses biblical examples, such as Naboth and Moses, to illustrate that true faithfulness involves staying committed to one's role, even when faced with challenges or the allure of promotions. The key takeaway is that God equips us for our assigned tasks and that we must trust Him to provide grace in difficult situations.

title: What Good Is Your Christianity?
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The True Measure of Faith
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen challenges listeners to examine the authenticity of their faith by asking the question, 'What seek ye?' He emphasizes that many people follow Jesus for personal benefits rather than a true desire for spiritual growth and transformation. The key takeaway is that a faith that does not lead to personal change and sanctification is not a saving faith.

title: When God Gets Tired
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: When God Grows Weary: Understanding Our Responsibilities
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores the theme of God's weariness with His people as described in Malachi. He emphasizes that while God has called Israel to a privileged position as His representatives, their fatigue with His requirements leads to His own weariness. The key takeaway is that God's love is not merely unconditional acceptance but encompasses His law and correction, which are essential for maintaining a relationship with Him. The sermon serves as a warning against becoming complacent in faith and neglecting the responsibilities that come with being God's chosen people.

title: The Kingdom NOT Of This World
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Divine Kingdom: Understanding Christ's Authority
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores the concept of Jesus' kingdom not being of this world, emphasizing that it is a divine kingdom characterized by meekness, justice, and righteousness. He argues that while Jesus' kingdom is not established through worldly means, it will ultimately manifest on earth with authority and order, contrasting the values of God's kingdom with those of the world. The takeaway is that believers are called to embody the meekness of Christ and ensure that God's purposes are fulfilled in their lives.

title: The Mind That Finds God
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Pursuit of the Mind That Seeks God
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen emphasizes the importance of having the right mindset to truly find God and grow in faith. He contrasts the noble Bereans, who actively sought the truth, with those who cling to erroneous beliefs, illustrating that one's mental attitude significantly impacts their spiritual journey. The key takeaway is that a sincere desire to seek truth and a willingness to change are essential for spiritual maturity and ultimately finding the 'pearl of great price' in Christ.

title: Noble Position Or Noble Person?
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The True Meaning of Nobility: Character vs. Position
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen contrasts the nobility of character with the nobility of position, using the examples of the Bereans and Thessalonians from Acts 17. He argues that true nobility is found in a willingness to seek truth and study the Scriptures, rather than resting on inherited beliefs or positions of power. The key takeaway is the importance of maintaining a noble heart towards God and truth, which allows for spiritual growth and understanding.

title: The Wise Use Of Youth
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Maximizing the Potential of Youth
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen addresses the importance of wisely using one's youth, particularly focusing on young people. He emphasizes that without a purposeful plan for growth and education, youth can easily slip into foolishness and mediocrity. The key takeaway is that young people must actively engage in learning and character development to avoid the pitfalls of a lazy and rebellious society, and that the discipline learned in youth will serve them well in adulthood.

title: Do You Have A Relationship With God?
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Understanding Your Relationship with God
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen emphasizes the importance of having a genuine personal relationship with God, arguing that many people mistakenly believe they have such a relationship without truly understanding its requirements. He outlines four foundational principles necessary for maintaining this relationship: mutual recognition by both parties, genuine love, not befriending God's enemies, and the necessity of agreement. The takeaway is that true relationship with God requires sincerity, commitment, and alignment with His will.

title: Where In This World Are We? Pt 2
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Finding Hope in a Troubled World
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen discusses the sovereignty of God amidst human suffering and the importance of free will in our choices. He emphasizes that while God has predetermined the bounds of our habitation, it is our responsibility to seek Him and make choices that align with His will. The message conveys hope for redemption and the ultimate victory of God's kingdom over evil, encouraging believers to remain steadfast in faith despite worldly challenges.
series: Where in This World Are We

title: Where In This World Are We? Pt 1
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Understanding Our Place in God's Timeline
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores the prophetic visions from the Book of Daniel, emphasizing the significance of understanding where we stand in God's timeline. He argues that we are living in the latter days of the fourth kingdom, which is characterized by political turmoil and the anticipation of Christ's return. The key takeaway is that believers should not be discouraged by current events but rather find hope and purpose in the promise of Christ's eternal kingdom that will ultimately prevail over all earthly powers.
series: Where in This World Are We

title: God's Hedge
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Understanding God's Protective Hedge
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores the concept of God's protective hedge as illustrated in the story of Job. He emphasizes that Job's godly character and commitment to God allowed him to be hedged in by divine protection, which was essential for his prosperity and safety. The sermon serves as a reminder that maintaining a relationship with God is crucial for spiritual protection against the adversary's attacks, and that authority structures also serve as hedges in our lives.

title: Galatians 6
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Restoration and Responsibility in the Spirit
summary: In this sermon on Galatians 6, Mark Bullen emphasizes the importance of restoring those who have been led astray by false teachings with a spirit of meekness and humility. He discusses the distinction between the deceiver and the deceived, urging believers to bear one another's burdens and to examine their own lives before judging others. The key takeaway is that true spiritual maturity involves recognizing one's own weaknesses and helping others with compassion, while also understanding the consequences of sowing to the flesh versus sowing to the spirit.

title: Galatians 5
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Freedom in Christ: Walking in the Spirit
summary: In this sermon on Galatians 5, Mark Bullen emphasizes the freedom Christians have in Christ, contrasting it with the bondage of the law and Judaism. He argues that justification comes solely through faith in Jesus, not through adherence to the law or Jewish customs. The key takeaway is that believers are called to walk in the Spirit and serve one another in love, rather than being entangled in legalism or the flesh.

title: Galatians 4
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: From Servants to Sons: Understanding Our Identity in Christ
summary: In this sermon on Galatians 4, Mark Bullen emphasizes the importance of understanding the transition from the Old Covenant, represented by the Mosaic Law, to the New Covenant established through Christ. He argues that the Old Testament served as a necessary educational tool, preparing believers to appreciate the significance of Christ's sacrifice and priesthood. The key takeaway is that true sonship in God's family comes through embracing Christ and His teachings, rather than reverting to the rituals of the Old Covenant.

title: Galatians 3
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Justification by Faith: The Message of Galatians 3
summary: In this sermon on Galatians 3, Mark Bullen emphasizes the importance of understanding justification by faith as taught by Paul. He argues against the reliance on the law for salvation, asserting that true faith, like that of Abraham, is characterized by obedience and trust in God's promises. The key takeaway is that believers, both Jews and Gentiles, are justified by faith in Christ, not by adherence to the law.

title: Galatians 2:11-21
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Understanding Justification: Faith Over Law
summary: In this sermon on Galatians 2:11-21, Mark Bullen emphasizes the importance of understanding the Jewish context of Jesus and the Apostles to avoid false teachings and legalism. He discusses the conflict between Peter and Paul regarding the inclusion of Gentiles and the implications of adhering to the law for justification. The key takeaway is that true justification comes through faith in Christ, not through the works of the law, and that believers must seek to live in accordance with God's moral law while relying on Christ's atonement.

title: Galatians 1:15 - 2:10
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The True Gospel: Understanding Paul's Authority
summary: In this sermon on Galatians 1:15 - 2:10, Mark Bullen emphasizes the importance of understanding the true gospel as preached by the Apostle Paul, warning against the dangers of accepting distorted versions of the gospel. He highlights Paul's authority as an apostle, which is rooted in a personal revelation from Jesus Christ rather than human tradition. The key takeaway is the necessity of verifying one's beliefs against the original teachings of scripture to avoid spiritual deception.

title: Intro To Galatians: New Covenant
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Understanding the New Covenant: A Deeper Look at Galatians
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores the concept of the New Covenant as presented in the Book of Galatians, emphasizing the distinction between the moral and ceremonial aspects of the law. He argues that the New Covenant is established with individuals who willingly accept God's law in their hearts, rather than with the nation of Israel as a whole. The key takeaway is that true believers, both Jews and Gentiles, are those who embrace God's moral law and have a personal relationship with Him, highlighting the importance of understanding the continuity of God's commandments throughout scripture.

title: Intro To Galatians: Earn Vs. Eligible
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Understanding Justification: The Balance of Faith and Obedience
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores the themes of justification and atonement as presented in Galatians, emphasizing the difference between being eligible for salvation and earning it through works. He argues that true justification comes through faith and obedience to God, rather than through the observance of the law or rituals. The key takeaway is that believers must maintain their justification by walking in the light and continually seeking forgiveness, rather than relying on a one-time act of faith.

title: The House Of Mourning
speaker: Jesse Herr
title_alt: The Wisdom Found in Mourning
summary: In this sermon, Jesse Herr emphasizes the importance of reflecting on mortality and the value of mourning as a means to gain wisdom and prepare for our own eventual death. He argues that the house of mourning offers insights and a sense of completeness that the house of feasting cannot provide, urging listeners to confront the reality of death to live more purposefully. The takeaway is that engaging with sorrow can lead to spiritual growth and a deeper understanding of life’s purpose.

title: No Vision?
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Importance of Divine Vision
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores Proverbs 29:18, emphasizing the importance of divine revelation and moral guidance in the Christian life. He argues that without a heavenly vision, people can lose sight of God's overarching plan, leading to moral failure. The key takeaway is that while a prophetic vision is valuable, adhering to God's law provides the necessary guidance and happiness, regardless of one's understanding of the big picture.

title: My Ebenezer
speaker: Philip Herr
title_alt: Hitherto Hath the Lord Helped Us
summary: In this sermon, Philip Herr reflects on the significance of raising an 'Ebenezer' as a reminder of God's help and guidance throughout life's challenges. He draws from the biblical account in 1 Samuel 7, emphasizing the importance of turning away from idols and relying on God's strength in times of trial. The key takeaway is that while struggles and temptations may persist, God has been faithful in the past and will continue to provide support for those who trust in Him.

title: Building OUR Ark
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Preparing Our Ark: Lessons from Noah
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen draws parallels between the days of Noah and the present, emphasizing the need for believers to build their own 'ark' through faith and obedience to God's word. He argues that just as Noah found grace by diligently seeking God and following His instructions, modern Christians must also engage actively in their faith to be eligible for God's grace and salvation. The takeaway is that building a strong, biblical community is essential for spiritual survival in the face of impending judgment.

title: 2 Timothy 4
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Staying Engaged in Faith Amidst Challenges
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen emphasizes the importance of maintaining a strong spiritual routine and being engaged in one's faith, drawing parallels between the biblical account of Esther and contemporary challenges faced by Christians. He urges believers to preach the Word and remain steadfast in sound doctrine, warning against the allure of false teachings that compromise true faith. The key takeaway is the call to be vigilant and proactive in living out one's faith, especially in the face of societal pressures and distractions.

title: 2 Timothy 3
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Perilous Times: A Call to Faithfulness
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen discusses the warnings of the Apostle Paul in 2 Timothy 3 about the moral decay and apostasy that will characterize the last days. He emphasizes the dangers of self-love, materialism, and the rejection of sound doctrine, which lead to a corrupt form of Christianity. The key takeaway is the importance of remaining steadfast in true faith and doctrine amidst a society that is increasingly turning away from God.

title: 2 Timothy 2:14-26
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Rightly Dividing the Word: A Call to Sound Doctrine
summary: In this sermon on 2 Timothy 2:14-26, Mark Bullen emphasizes the importance of focusing on sound doctrine and avoiding unprofitable arguments that lead to division within the church. He urges believers to study the Word of God diligently to rightly divide truth from error, highlighting the dangers of false teachings and the necessity of maintaining purity in doctrine. The key takeaway is that while some issues may seem trivial, the integrity of the Gospel and the unity of the church are worth fighting for.

title: 2 Timothy 2:1-13
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Strength in Grace: Lessons for Ministry from 2 Timothy 2
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen emphasizes the importance of being strong in the grace of Christ Jesus, particularly for ministers like Timothy. He discusses the necessity of enduring hardships as a soldier of Christ, adhering to the principles of the faith once delivered, and the responsibilities of church leaders to preserve and pass on sound doctrine. The takeaway is that true strength and success in ministry come from remaining steadfast in God's grace and fulfilling one's calling without compromise.

title: 2 Timothy Chapter One
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Courage in the Face of Persecution: Lessons from 2 Timothy
summary: In this sermon on 2 Timothy Chapter One, Mark Bullen explores the context of Paul's imprisonment and his relationship with Timothy, emphasizing the importance of courage and faith in the face of persecution. He highlights Paul's encouragement to Timothy to rekindle his spiritual gifts and not to be ashamed of the gospel, even as Christians faced severe trials under Nero's rule. The takeaway is a call to embrace one's faith boldly and to recognize the value of suffering for Christ as a means to eternal glory.

title: Watch Your Wanter
speaker: Philip Herr
title_alt: Guard Your Heart: The Power of Your Desires
summary: In this sermon, Philip Herr emphasizes the importance of being mindful of our desires, or 'wanters,' as they shape our actions and ultimately our destinies. He uses the story of Baelim from Numbers 22 to illustrate how our hearts can lead us astray when we prioritize our own desires over God's will. The key takeaway is to examine what we truly want and ensure that our goals align with godliness, as this will guide us toward a fulfilling and righteous life.

title: I Timothy 6
speaker: Mark Bullen

He begins with servants under the yoke counting their masters “worthy of all honour,” arguing the gospel changes the heart rather than a person's civil or financial station, and rebukes a “welfare mentality” that expects the church to absolve debts and set up new converts in business. From verses 3-10 he exposes those who suppose “gain is godliness,” insisting prosperity is not proof of God's blessing, citing Lazarus, Joseph, and Daniel as godly men in low estate, and warning that “the love of money is the root of all evil.” He presses Timothy to “flee these things,” “fight the good fig

guarding the deposit of sound doctrine

title: I Timothy 4
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Beware of Seducing Spirits: A Call to Sound Doctrine
summary: In this sermon on I Timothy 4, Mark Bullen warns against the dangers of seducing spirits and doctrines of devils that lead many away from the true faith. He emphasizes the importance of sound doctrine and the need for believers to be vigilant against false teachings that can corrupt their understanding of Christianity. The key takeaway is the necessity of grounding oneself in the Word of God and being aware of the subtle ways in which false doctrines can infiltrate the church.

title: I Timothy 3:8-16
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Pillar and Ground of Truth: Qualifications for Church Leadership
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen emphasizes the importance of adhering to God's order and qualifications for church leadership, particularly focusing on the roles of bishops and deacons as outlined in 1 Timothy 3:8-16. He argues that a genuine relationship with God requires obedience to His terms, and that church leaders must exemplify seriousness, integrity, and a commitment to the faith. The takeaway is that the church must uphold its role as the pillar and ground of truth, prioritizing doctrinal fidelity over cultural relevance.

title: I Timothy 3
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Striving for Godly Leadership: Lessons from 1 Timothy 3
summary: In this sermon on 1 Timothy 3, Mark Bullen emphasizes the importance of character qualifications for church leaders, specifically bishops and deacons, as representatives of the church membership. He argues that aspiring to leadership should be seen positively, as it reflects a desire to serve and uphold the faith. The takeaway is that all church members should strive for the character traits outlined in scripture, as these qualities are essential for effective leadership and the health of the church.

title: I Timothy 2:11-15
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Understanding Biblical Roles: Men, Women, and Authority
summary: In this sermon on 1 Timothy 2:11-15, Mark Bullen emphasizes the biblical roles of men and women, arguing that women should learn in silence and not usurp authority over men in the church. He presents three reasons for this order: the order of creation, the purpose of creation, and the fact that Eve was deceived. The key takeaway is that fulfilling one's God-given role is a matter of protection and efficiency in spiritual matters, rather than a question of equality.

title: True & False Grace
speaker: Nathan Bullen
title_alt: Understanding Grace: The Law of Works vs. The Law of Faith
summary: In this sermon, Nathan Bullen teaches on 'the law of works versus the law of faith' from Romans 3:27, using the message partly to model how he studies — fixing 'foundation stones' (God does not change, God cannot lie, Scripture is God's own word) and reading whole passages rather than isolating verses. Against Marcionism and dispensationalism, he argues that the Old Covenant was never 'the law of works': Abraham, David, Noah, and Moses were all saved by grace through faith exactly as believers are now, and the 'law of works' is simply the false hope of justifying oneself by one's own system or effort, which no flesh can do. title: I Timothy 1:17-2:10
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Holding Faith with a Pure Conscience
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen emphasizes the importance of holding onto the faith with a pure conscience, as exemplified by Timothy's ordination and the dangers of straying from this path. He warns against using faith for personal gain, which leads to spiritual shipwreck, and stresses the necessity of prayer for leaders to maintain a godly and peaceful life. The message culminates in the call for men to pray with holy hands and for women to embody modesty, reflecting the character of a true Christian community.

title: I Timothy 1:1-17
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Charge to Timothy: Upholding Sound Doctrine
summary: In this sermon on 1 Timothy 1:1-17, Mark Bullen emphasizes the importance of sound doctrine and the role of Timothy as a young pastor. He discusses the charge given to Timothy by Paul, highlighting that the ultimate goal of ministry is to produce God's love in the hearts of believers. The sermon warns against false teachings and underscores the significance of understanding God's law as a reflection of His love, urging the congregation to maintain a clear conscience and sincere faith.

title: 2 Corinthians 13
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Importance of Witnesses and Self-Examination in the Church
summary: In this sermon on 2 Corinthians 13, Mark Bullen emphasizes the importance of adhering to the entirety of Scripture and the principles of church discipline. He discusses the necessity of having multiple witnesses in judicial proceedings within the church, drawing parallels to biblical practices. The key takeaway is the call for self-examination among believers to ensure they are living in accordance with their faith, rather than relying on personal biases or experiences.

title: 2 Corinthians 12
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Strength in Weakness: Lessons from Paul's Thorn
summary: In this sermon on 2 Corinthians 12, Mark Bullen explores the Apostle Paul's experiences of suffering and the significance of his visions, particularly his encounter with the third heaven. He emphasizes that Paul's thorn in the flesh served to keep him humble and reliant on God's grace, illustrating that true strength comes through weakness. The takeaway is that believers should embrace their challenges as opportunities for growth and deeper reliance on Christ.

title: 2 Corinthians 11
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Defending the True Gospel: Paul's Warning Against Deception
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores 2 Corinthians 11, emphasizing Paul's defense of his apostleship against false teachers who distort the gospel. He draws parallels between the biblical story of Abraham's servant seeking a bride for Isaac and the church's relationship with Christ, warning against the dangers of following a 'different Jesus' and the subtlety of deception. The key takeaway is the importance of maintaining a pure and singular devotion to Christ, avoiding the allure of false teachings and gospels.

title: 2 Corinthians 10
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Defending True Apostolic Authority
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen discusses Paul's defense of his apostleship in 2 Corinthians 10, emphasizing the importance of spiritual authority over worldly values and eloquence. He critiques false teachers who manipulate and distort the truth for personal gain, contrasting their approach with Paul's meekness and gentleness, which he argues is rooted in Christ's character. The key takeaway is the necessity of discerning true spiritual authority and the dangers of succumbing to false teachings that prioritize appearance over substance.

title: 2 Corinthians 8-9
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Grace of Generosity: Lessons from 2 Corinthians 8-9
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores the themes of grace and generosity as illustrated in 2 Corinthians 8-9, emphasizing that true giving stems from a heart transformed by God's grace. He highlights the example of the Macedonian churches, who, despite their poverty, exhibited remarkable generosity, demonstrating that the intentions behind giving are what truly matter to God. The takeaway is that genuine faith leads to a desire to give and support others, reflecting the grace received from God.

title: 2 Corinthians 7
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Good News of Holiness and Repentance
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen emphasizes the importance of recognizing and valuing God's promises, which call believers to a life of holiness and separation from sin. He argues that true repentance involves a heartfelt turning back to God, which is essential for salvation and spiritual transformation. The takeaway is that embracing God's promises and the call to holiness should be seen as good news, motivating believers to pursue a deeper relationship with God.

title: 2 Corinthians 6
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Ambassadors for Christ: The Call to Faithful Representation
summary: In this sermon on 2 Corinthians 6, Mark Bullen emphasizes the responsibility of Christians as ambassadors for Christ, urging believers to recognize their role in representing God accurately. He warns against the dangers of receiving God's grace in vain and highlights the importance of maintaining a pure relationship with God, free from the influence of false teachings and worldly associations. The key takeaway is the necessity of actively engaging with one's faith and being mindful of how one's actions reflect on the ministry.

title: 2 Corinthians 5
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Eternal Bodies: Understanding Life After Death
summary: In this sermon on 2 Corinthians 5, Mark Bullen emphasizes the distinction between our earthly bodies and the eternal bodies we will receive at resurrection. He argues against the concept of soul sleep, asserting that believers are conscious after death and awaiting their resurrection. The key takeaway is the importance of living a life that is pleasing to God, as our actions in the body will be judged, and we should labor to be accepted by Him.

title: 2 Corinthians 4
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Embracing Wisdom Through Suffering
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen emphasizes the importance of wisdom as finding and living in God's will throughout life, using 2 Corinthians 4 to illustrate the apostle Paul's perspective on suffering and ministry. He argues that true wisdom involves recognizing trials as mercies from God, which shape us and allow us to manifest Christ's life in our own. The key takeaway is that enduring hardships for the sake of the gospel is a privilege and a part of God's purpose for believers.

title: 2 Corinthians 3
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Transformative Power of the New Covenant
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores 2 Corinthians 3, emphasizing the Apostle Paul's defense against criticism and his assertion that true endorsement comes from Christ rather than letters of commendation. He argues that the New Covenant, characterized by the Spirit, surpasses the Old Covenant, which was a mere administration of death. The key takeaway is that believers are empowered by the Spirit to fulfill God's law, which is now written on their hearts, highlighting the transformative power of grace in the life of a Christian.

title: 2 Corinthians 2
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Sweet Savor of Christ: Leadership, Discipline, and Forgiveness
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores the Apostle Paul's letter to the Corinthians, emphasizing the importance of church authority, discipline, and the need for genuine repentance and forgiveness. Paul expresses his anguish over the church's struggles and the necessity of confronting sin to prevent Satan from gaining an advantage. The key takeaway is that true leadership in the church is rooted in love and a desire to guide others toward spiritual health, while also recognizing the personal responsibility of each believer in responding to God's truth.

title: 2 Corinthians 1
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Purpose of Suffering: Building Bridges Through Tribulation
summary: In this sermon on 2 Corinthians 1, Mark Bullen explores the Apostle Paul's experiences of suffering and comfort, emphasizing that tribulations are a necessary part of the Christian journey. He argues that suffering not only strengthens believers but also equips them to comfort others in their struggles. The key takeaway is that suffering is integral to spiritual growth and should be viewed as an opportunity to build bridges of support for others.

title: I Corinthians 16
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Heart of Paul's Letters: Generosity and Unity in the Church
summary: In this sermon on 1 Corinthians 16, Mark Bullen emphasizes the importance of the Apostle Paul's letters as personal and direct communications to specific churches, addressing their needs and challenges. He discusses the significance of the collection for the poor saints in Jerusalem, highlighting the unity and support among the early churches, particularly between Gentile and Jewish believers. The takeaway is the call to generosity, the joy of giving, and the importance of standing firm in faith amidst adversity.

title: I Corinthians 15 - Resurrection (Part Two)
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Assurance of Resurrection: Hope Beyond the Grave
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen emphasizes the critical importance of the resurrection as outlined in 1 Corinthians 15. He argues that denying the resurrection undermines the entire Christian faith, rendering preaching and faith in vain. The message highlights that Christ's resurrection assures believers of their own future resurrection and the justice of God, reinforcing the hope that their labor in the Lord is not in vain. The takeaway is a call to live in covenant with Christ, embracing the hope of resurrection and eternal life.

title: I Corinthians 15 - Resurrection
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Essential Resurrection: Hope Beyond Suffering
summary: In this sermon on I Corinthians 15, Mark Bullen emphasizes the critical importance of the resurrection of Jesus Christ to the Christian faith. He argues that without the resurrection, the apostles, including Paul, would be the most miserable of all people for their sacrifices and sufferings. The sermon highlights that belief in the resurrection is essential for salvation and that grace must be actively retained and acted upon to avoid believing in vain.

title: I Corinthians 14 - The Abuse Of Gifts
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Understanding Spiritual Gifts: The True Purpose of Tongues
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen addresses the misuse and misunderstanding of spiritual gifts, particularly the gift of tongues, as discussed in 1 Corinthians 14. He emphasizes that these gifts should be used for the edification of the church rather than for personal display or confusion. The main takeaway is that true spirituality is rooted in love and understanding, and that communication in a known language is essential for building up the church community.

title: I Corinthians 13 - LOVE
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Essence of Love in 1 Corinthians 13
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen emphasizes the importance of true Christian love as outlined in 1 Corinthians 13, contrasting it with superficial spirituality. He argues that spiritual gifts are meaningless without love, which should be the guiding principle in a believer's life. The takeaway is that love, as defined by God's character, is essential for genuine worship and relationships, and that believers must evaluate their actions through the lens of God's love rather than their own understanding.

title: I Corinthians 12
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Discerning True Spirituality: Understanding 1 Corinthians 12
summary: In this sermon on 1 Corinthians 12, Mark Bullen emphasizes the importance of discerning between true and false spiritual manifestations within the church. He explains that not all spiritual gifts are from God and warns against being misled by false teachings and practices that mimic true spirituality. The key takeaway is the necessity of understanding and recognizing the true nature of spiritual gifts and the unity of the body of Christ, which requires each member to fulfill their God-given role.
themes: unity of the body of Christ

title: I Corinthians 11 - Holy Communion
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Understanding the Significance of Holy Communion
summary: In this sermon on I Corinthians 11, Mark Bullen discusses the significance of Holy Communion and the importance of partaking in it worthily. He emphasizes that Communion is a gift from God meant to encourage believers to remember Christ's sacrifice, rather than a ritual that can lead to condemnation if approached improperly. The key takeaway is the necessity of self-examination and proper reverence when participating in Communion, as it reflects one's relationship with God and the church community.

title: Dealing With Infirmities
speaker: Philip Herr
title_alt: Embracing Human Infirmities with Compassion
summary: In this sermon, Philip Herr discusses the importance of understanding and dealing with human infirmities as illustrated through the story of Saul and Jonathan in 1 Samuel 14. He highlights Saul's rash decisions and lack of compassion, contrasting it with Jonathan's faith and trust in God. The key takeaway is the need for mercy and understanding towards others' shortcomings, recognizing that everyone has limitations and that God desires compassion over strict adherence to rules.

title: I Corinthians 11 - Headcovering
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Importance of Head Coverings: Authority and Modesty in Worship
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen discusses the significance of head coverings in the context of 1 Corinthians 11, emphasizing the importance of maintaining proper order and authority in worship. He argues that the liberties Christians take should not lead to the downfall of others, highlighting the responsibility believers have towards one another's spiritual well-being. The takeaway is that Christians must live in a way that honors God and supports the faith of others, particularly in a culture that often blurs the lines of modesty and authority.

title: I Corinthians Chapter 10
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Liberty and Responsibility: Lessons from 1 Corinthians 10
summary: In this sermon on 1 Corinthians chapter 10, Mark Bullen emphasizes the importance of understanding Christian liberty in the context of community and the testimony of the Church. He argues that the Corinthians were misusing their freedom by prioritizing personal desires over the spiritual well-being of others, drawing parallels to the Israelites' failures in the wilderness. The key takeaway is the call to seek God's heart and to prioritize the advancement of His Kingdom over individual liberties.

title: I Corinthians Chapter 9 Part 2
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Understanding Marriage and Authority in the New Covenant
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores the teachings of Paul in 1 Corinthians Chapter 9, emphasizing the contrast between the Old Testament law and the New Testament gospel. He argues that the law led many to spiritual death due to its lack of power to enable righteous living, while the gospel provides the necessary strength for believers. Bullen addresses issues of marriage, celibacy, and church authority, highlighting the importance of understanding God's design for relationships and the role of the church in guiding believers.

title: I Corinthians Chapters 8-9
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Understanding Liberty and Responsibility in Christ
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores the themes of knowledge, liberty, and responsibility within the context of 1 Corinthians chapters 8 and 9. He emphasizes that true Christian knowledge is demonstrated through love and consideration for others, particularly the weak in faith. The takeaway is that believers should prioritize the well-being of others over personal freedoms, as exercising liberty without regard for others can lead to spiritual harm and division within the church.

title: I Corinthians Chapter 7-2
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Running the Race of Faith: Beyond Minimal Effort
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores the Apostle Paul's teachings in 1 Corinthians 9, emphasizing the importance of self-sacrifice and dedication in the Christian life. He argues that true knowledge of God leads to a life of service and that believers should view their blessings as obligations to serve more fervently. The key takeaway is that Christians must strive for spiritual excellence, not merely settle for minimal effort, as they run the race of faith towards eternal rewards.

title: I Corinthians Chapter 7
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Understanding Marriage and Divorce in 1 Corinthians 7
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen discusses the teachings of 1 Corinthians 7, addressing issues of marriage, divorce, and celibacy in the context of a licentious society. He emphasizes the importance of adhering to biblical truth amidst various interpretations and doctrines that distort the original message. The key takeaway is that marriage is a God-ordained institution, and believers should seek to understand and follow God's law regarding relationships, rather than succumbing to cultural pressures or erroneous teachings.

title: I Corinthians Chapter 6
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Judging Righteousness: Lessons from I Corinthians 6
summary: In this sermon on I Corinthians Chapter 6, Mark Bullen emphasizes the importance of addressing root problems within the church rather than merely treating symptoms. He critiques the Corinthian believers for their misguided sense of superiority and their failure to judge matters within their community, urging them to recognize that unrighteousness will prevent them from inheriting the kingdom of God. The key takeaway is the call to self-examination and the understanding that true Christian love and conduct must align with God's standards, rather than personal or societal norms.

title: I Corinthians Chapter 5-6
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Addressing Immaturity and Sin in the Church
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen discusses the issues of immaturity and sin within the Corinthian church as addressed by Paul in 1 Corinthians chapters 5 and 6. He emphasizes the dangers of a puffed-up attitude among believers who overlook their own dysfunction while judging others. The sermon underscores the importance of church discipline and the need for a biblical understanding of justice, urging congregants to maintain moral integrity and accountability within the church community.

title: Harlot Or Bride?
speaker: Philip Herr
title_alt: The Virtuous Woman vs. The Harlot: A Call to Faithfulness
summary: The sermon contrasts the virtuous woman of Proverbs 31 with the harlot of Proverbs 7 and Revelation 17, emphasizing the importance of wisdom, kindness, and genuine care in relationships and faith. The speaker argues that true faithfulness to God is demonstrated through actions and character, rather than mere outward appearances or flattery. The takeaway is a call to embody the virtues of the bride of Christ, being faithful and industrious in both personal and spiritual lives.

title: Tithing In The New Testament?
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Understanding Tithing: A Biblical Perspective
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen addresses the topic of tithing in the New Testament, emphasizing its biblical roots in the practices of Abraham and Jacob. He argues that tithing is a principle of gratitude and acknowledgment of God's provision, which has been historically significant in the relationship between God and His people. The takeaway is that while the New Covenant may not explicitly mandate tithing, the spirit of giving and supporting God's work remains essential for believers.

title: I Corinthians Chapter Four
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The True Measure of Faithfulness
summary: In this sermon on 1 Corinthians Chapter 4, Mark Bullen emphasizes the importance of true stewardship and faithfulness in the Christian life, contrasting the superficial wisdom of the Corinthian church with the genuine struggles and sacrifices of the apostles. He warns against pride and self-evaluation, reminding the congregation that true judgment belongs to God alone. The key takeaway is that faithfulness, rather than accomplishments or appearances, is what truly matters in the eyes of God.

title: I Corinthians Chapter Two
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Understanding God's Wisdom vs. Human Wisdom
summary: In this sermon on 1 Corinthians chapter 2, Mark Bullen emphasizes the contrast between human wisdom and God's wisdom, highlighting the importance of aligning one's goals (point B) with God's intentions. He critiques the Corinthian church for their immaturity and misguided judgments of the apostles, urging them to seek true spiritual maturity through the mind of Christ. The takeaway is that true wisdom and success in the Christian life come from understanding and pursuing God's values rather than worldly standards.

title: I Corinthians Chapter One
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Seeing God in Everyday Life
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen discusses the subtle ways God works in our lives, often through natural circumstances rather than overt miracles. He emphasizes the importance of seeking God personally and recognizing His presence in our experiences, despite skepticism from others. The message encourages believers to focus on their relationship with God and to understand that true wisdom comes from humility and faith rather than worldly standards.

title: The Father's Vision
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Embracing the Father's Vision for the Home
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores the parable of the Prodigal Son to illustrate the importance of understanding and embracing the Father's vision for the home. He emphasizes that God's household is structured for the benefit of all, where rules and responsibilities lead to a productive and fulfilling life. The takeaway is that true repentance and fulfillment come from recognizing the wisdom of the Father's ways, rather than focusing on personal grievances or shortcomings.

title: Did God Want Jews To Become Gentiles?
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Understanding the Early Church: Jews, Gentiles, and the Law
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores the complexities surrounding the relationship between Jewish and Gentile believers in the early church, particularly focusing on Acts 21. He argues against the notion that Jewish Christians were to abandon the Mosaic law, emphasizing that the apostles, including Paul, maintained their Jewish identity and practices while also welcoming Gentiles into the faith. The key takeaway is the importance of understanding the historical and theological context of the early church's decisions regarding the law and grace.

title: What Is Success?
speaker: Jesse Herr
title_alt: Redefining Success: Lessons from Lazarus and the Rich Man
summary: In the sermon 'What Is Success?', Jesse Herr explores the contrasting lives of a rich man and Lazarus from Luke 16, emphasizing that true success is not defined by wealth or social status but by one's relationship with God and adherence to His commandments. The rich man, despite his earthly success, ends up in torment because he lived for himself rather than for God, while Lazarus, who suffered in life, finds comfort in eternity due to his faithfulness. The key takeaway is that true success is found in godliness and living according to God's will, rather than in material wealth or societal esteem.

title: Is Christianity Hard Or Easy?
speaker: Philip Herr
title_alt: The Paradox of Christianity: Easy Burdens and Hard Choices
summary: In this sermon, Philip Herr explores the paradox of Christianity being both easy and hard, as presented in scripture. He emphasizes that true Christian living requires a willingness to die to oneself, which leads to true life and fulfillment. The key takeaway is that while the Christian journey involves challenges and sacrifices, it ultimately offers rest and purpose through a relationship with Christ.

title: Recipe For A Good Report
speaker: Nathan Bullen
title_alt: Living for a Good Report: The Recipe for Faithfulness
summary: In this sermon, Nathan Bullen emphasizes the importance of living a life that will yield a good report before God, akin to the heroes of the Bible. He encourages listeners to make daily choices that align with faith and obedience, stressing that true faith is demonstrated through actions, especially during trials. The key takeaway is that anyone can achieve a commendable report in their spiritual journey by adhering to God's principles and maintaining a steadfast commitment to their faith.

title: Who Is A Wise Man?
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The True Nature of Wisdom
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores the concept of true wisdom as outlined in James 3:13 and Proverbs 31:28, contrasting earthly wisdom with wisdom from above. He emphasizes that true wisdom is demonstrated through good conduct and humility, rather than self-assertion and envy. The takeaway is that genuine wisdom leads to a life that reflects God's standards and ultimately results in praise from others, while the pursuit of worldly wisdom can lead to spiritual downfall.

title: Living Faith Christian Fellowship - WHY?
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Understanding Our Purpose: The Why Behind Living Faith Christian Fellowship
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen addresses the foundational question of why Living Faith Christian Fellowship exists amidst a multitude of churches. He emphasizes the importance of understanding biblical doctrine and the need for a clear vision in faith. Bullen critiques the tendency of modern Christianity to stray from God's commandments and warns against the complacency that leads to spiritual decline, urging listeners to earnestly contend for the faith once delivered to the saints.

title: The Foundation Of Moral Courage
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Power of Resurrection: Building Moral Courage
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen emphasizes the foundational role of the resurrection in Christian faith, arguing that it provides moral courage and hope in the face of death. He discusses how the apostles' encounters with the resurrected Christ transformed their fear of death into boldness, enabling them to endure persecution and suffering. The takeaway is that belief in the resurrection is essential for living a life of integrity and courage, as it assures believers of eternal life and divine justice.

title: Path To Deception - Part 2
speaker: Jesse Herr
title_alt: The Dangers of Deception: A Call to Genuine Faith
summary: In this sermon, Jesse Herr explores the theme of deception, emphasizing how self-love and a lack of genuine faith can lead individuals away from the truth of God's word. He argues that true belief in God transforms one's nature and leads to obedience, while shallow faith results in a reliance on peer approval rather than divine truth. The takeaway is a call for self-examination to ensure one's faith is rooted in a sincere relationship with God, rather than mere adherence to tradition or societal expectations.

title: Street Smart
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Navigating Life with Street Smarts
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen emphasizes the importance of being 'street smart' in navigating life's challenges, particularly in relation to spiritual and moral decisions. He uses Proverbs 7 to illustrate the dangers of naivety and the consequences of ignoring wisdom. The key takeaway is that knowledge alone is not enough; one must also possess the discernment and experience to recognize and avoid potential pitfalls in life.

title: Key To A God Honoring Marriage
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Divine Blueprint for Marriage
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen emphasizes the importance of understanding the roles of authority and influence within a God-honoring marriage, drawing from Ephesians 5 and examples from the lives of Abigail and Michael. He argues that husbands should love their wives selflessly, while wives should influence their husbands positively, aligning with God's design. The key takeaway is that both partners must seek God's guidance and maintain a humble, prayerful attitude to fulfill their roles effectively.

title: The Voice Of The LORD Calling
speaker: Philip Herr
title_alt: Responding to the Call of God
summary: The sermon explores the theme of God's call to His people, emphasizing the importance of responding to His voice and maintaining a close relationship with Him. Using the allegory from the Song of Solomon and examples from the lives of Saul, David, and Jonah, the speaker illustrates how reluctance and disobedience can lead to a withdrawal of God's presence. The key takeaway is the necessity of seeking reconciliation with God, even amidst suffering, and recognizing the tokens of His love that encourage us to return to Him.

title: Preparation For Deception
speaker: Jesse Herr
title_alt: Guarding Against Deception: Lessons from Revelation 20
summary: In this sermon, Jesse Herr explores Revelation 20, emphasizing the theme of deception and the nature of the human heart. He discusses how even after a thousand years of righteous rule, Satan's release reveals the underlying rebellion in people's hearts, leading them to follow him again. The sermon serves as a warning about the dangers of deception and the importance of cultivating knowledge and virtue to avoid falling into temptation.

title: Feathers Determine Flock
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Character Determines Community
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen emphasizes the importance of character development and the choices we make in life, illustrating that our 'feathers'—or character traits—determine the 'flock' we associate with. He uses Proverbs 1:29-32 to highlight the consequences of rejecting God's counsel and the dangers of following the crowd. The key takeaway is that the character we build will ultimately dictate our relationships and our eternal destiny, urging listeners to consciously choose to develop godly traits.

title: After 37 Years
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Harvest of the Heart: Lessons from 37 Years in Ministry
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen reflects on his 37 years of ministry and emphasizes the importance of understanding and applying the teachings of Jesus, particularly from the Sermon on the Mount. He argues that true obedience to God's law stems from a heart that loves the Lord, rather than mere adherence to rules. Bullen warns against the distractions of complex theology that can obscure the simple truths of Scripture, urging listeners to examine which 'harvest' they belong to—wheat or chaff—based on their love for God and righteousness.

title: Do You Care?
speaker: Philip Herr
title_alt: Do You Truly Care About Christ's Sacrifice?
summary: In this sermon, Philip Herr emphasizes the importance of recognizing the sacrifice of Jesus Christ and the need for believers to care about their relationship with God. He uses the metaphor of a train bridge operator who sacrifices his son to save others, illustrating how often people take for granted the life given for them. The key takeaway is to reflect on the cost of salvation and to respond with gratitude and a commitment to live in accordance with God's will.

title: The Good, The Bad, And The Yukidy
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Dynamics of Good, Bad, and Ugly in Life
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores the dynamics of good, bad, and ugly characters in the biblical narrative, particularly focusing on the story of David, Saul, and Jonathan. He emphasizes the importance of recognizing the different types of people one encounters in life—those who genuinely seek to do good, those who are indifferent, and those who actively oppose God's will. The takeaway is a call to discernment and integrity in one's own life, encouraging listeners to strive to be among the good while being aware of the influences of the bad and the ugly.

title: Bro. Jesse To Jim Polanek
speaker: Jesse Herr
title_alt: United in God's Purpose
summary: In this sermon, Jesse Herr reflects on the importance of unity and support among God's people, using biblical examples from Exodus, 1 Samuel, and Matthew. He emphasizes that true victory comes from collective reliance on God, as illustrated by Moses and the Israelites' battle against Amalek. The message encourages listeners to recognize their roles in God's plan, to support one another, and to be discerning in their alliances, ensuring they align with God's purposes rather than worldly agendas.

title: Characteristics Of Spiritual People
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Legacy of Jabez: Characteristics of a Spiritual Leader
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores the life of Jabez, emphasizing his honorable character and the legacy he left through his disciples. Jabez is portrayed as a man of prayer and action, who sought God's blessing and aimed to positively influence others, particularly the youth. The key takeaway is the importance of fervent prayer, worship, and the pursuit of holiness in the life of a believer, as exemplified by Jabez and his followers.

title: Escaping Pollution?
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Understanding True Liberty: Escaping the World's Pollution
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores the Apostle Peter's teachings on escaping the pollutions of the world and the dangers posed by false prophets. He emphasizes the importance of understanding true liberty as freedom from sin and error, contrasting it with the deceptive allure of worldly desires. The key takeaway is that genuine knowledge of the Lord empowers believers to resist temptation and live righteously, while neglecting this knowledge can lead to entrapment and spiritual blindness.

title: Exceeding Great Reward
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Choosing God as Your Portion
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen emphasizes the importance of choosing God as one's portion in life, contrasting the choices of Abraham and Lot. Abraham sought a relationship with God and prioritized spiritual over material wealth, while Lot pursued earthly comforts and riches, ultimately leading to his downfall. The key takeaway is that true fulfillment and inheritance come from God, not from worldly pursuits.

title: Beyond Pardon
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: From Pardon to Glory: The True Journey of Salvation
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen emphasizes that salvation is not merely about being pardoned from sin but about pursuing a deeper relationship with God that leads to glory. He argues that many Christians mistakenly believe that forgiveness is the ultimate goal, while in reality, it is just a means to an end—becoming conformed to the image of Christ and sharing in His glory. The key takeaway is that true salvation involves striving to overcome and fulfill God's purpose for our lives, which goes beyond mere acceptance into heaven.

title: Worth Remembering?
speaker: Jesse Herr
title_alt: Memories Worth Keeping
summary: In this sermon, Jesse Herr emphasizes the importance of remembering God's promises and our actions that align with His will. He uses biblical examples, such as Cornelius and Philip, to illustrate how God values our prayers and sacrifices, urging listeners to consider what they want to be remembered for. The key takeaway is to live in a way that reflects our faith and commitment to God, ensuring that our actions are worth remembering both by God and ourselves.

title: "Play-Like" Christianity?
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Growing Up in Faith: From Play to Purpose
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen emphasizes the distinction between 'play-like' Christianity and true adult Christianity, urging believers to mature in their faith and take their responsibilities seriously. He uses the story of Job to illustrate how God expects His servants to uphold His truth and integrity, even amidst trials. The key takeaway is that true faith requires a commitment to God's ways, rather than a superficial or self-serving approach to Christianity.

title: The Fear Of God
speaker: Philip Herr
title_alt: Understanding the Proper Fear of God
summary: In this sermon, Philip Herr discusses the concept of the fear of God, emphasizing that it should not be a paralyzing terror but a respectful reverence that leads to obedience. He contrasts the fear that brings torment with a healthy fear that acknowledges God's power and authority while also trusting in His love and grace. The takeaway is that true fear of God motivates believers to stay within His boundaries, fostering a relationship built on love and respect rather than dread.

title: The Secret To Success In God's Kingdom
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Understanding Success in God's Kingdom
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen explores the concept of success in God's Kingdom, emphasizing that true success comes from understanding and fulfilling one's God-given role within the larger body of Christ. He uses the story of King Uzziah to illustrate how pride and overstepping boundaries can lead to failure, and he encourages listeners to excel in their designated spots while respecting the divine order established by God. The key takeaway is that individual success is intertwined with the success of the whole body, and one must operate within their God-given boundaries to truly succeed.

title: Plan Your Funeral!
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Designing Your Legacy: A Call to Reflect
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen emphasizes the importance of planning one's legacy and funeral, urging listeners to reflect on what they want to be remembered for after their death. He draws from Ecclesiastes 12 to illustrate the inevitability of aging and death, encouraging the audience to consider their values, ethics, and the impact they will leave behind. The key takeaway is that one must intentionally design their legacy in alignment with God's truth to ensure a meaningful and honorable remembrance.

title: Body Dynamics
speaker: Philip Herr
title_alt: Unity in Diversity: Understanding the Body of Christ
summary: In this sermon, Philip Herr discusses the dynamics of the church as the body of Christ, emphasizing the importance of unity and the diverse roles each member plays. He highlights that every member, regardless of their perceived importance, contributes to the overall health and function of the church. The key takeaway is that all members should recognize their unique gifts and work together for the benefit of the body, fostering spiritual growth and maturity while avoiding divisions.

title: God's Doorkeepers
speaker: Jesse Herr
title_alt: The Importance of Faithful Doorkeeping
summary: In this sermon, Jesse Herr emphasizes the importance of being a faithful doorkeeper in God's house, drawing from biblical examples to illustrate the responsibilities and consequences of this role. He contrasts the privilege of serving God with the dangers of allowing defilement into one's life and community. The key takeaway is that every believer is called to be a doorkeeper, guarding against sin and promoting holiness in their lives and surroundings.

title: Thank You LORD!
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Honoring Parents and God: A Call to Gratitude
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen emphasizes the importance of honoring one's parents and recognizing the sacrifices they make, paralleling this with our relationship with God. He critiques the Pharisees for prioritizing traditions over the commandments of God, urging listeners to express gratitude for both parental figures and the Creator. The key takeaway is the call to appreciate and honor those who have invested in our lives, as well as to acknowledge God's gifts in our daily existence.

title: Meditations On Christ's Birth
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Divine Orchestration of Christ's Birth
summary: In this study, Mark Bullen leads a service of prophecy, Scripture, and hymns meditating on Christ's birth, delivered March 31, 2019. He frames the readings as one “multi-generational program” God carried out across 6,000 years regardless of which empires rose and fell. The congregation reads the seed promise of Genesis 3:15, Jacob's scepter (Genesis 49:10), Balaam's star (Numbers 24:17), Psalm 2, Isaiah 7:14, 9:6, and 53, Micah 5:2, Daniel 9:25, and the narratives of Matthew 1-2, Luke 2, John 1, and Philippians 2. Bullen notes the likely spring, lambing-season timing and refuses to exalt the birth above the resurrection. His closing meditation stresses that the nativity is documented history

title: The Doctrine Of Balaam-Lenin
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Perils of Compromise: Lessons from Balaam
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen studies the doctrine of Balaam from Numbers 23-25 and Revelation 2:14. Unable to curse a people walking with God, Balaam counsels Balak to seduce Israel through the Moabite women into idolatry and fornication so that God's justice would turn against them, and 24,000 die by plague. Bullen calls this Satan's Eden strategy and traces it through Deuteronomy 28, Isaiah 29:13, Nehemiah 9, and Jesus' warning about salt that loses its savor (Matthew 5:13). speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The True Nature of Christian Patriotism

Working from the Greek “patris,” he defines a true Christian patriot as “a grateful son” and good steward of what the fathers handed down, contrasting him with the prodigal who wasted his inheritance. Daniel, Joseph, Nehemiah, Mordecai, and Esther model faithful service that seeks a city's peace (Jeremiah 29:7) and influences rulers toward God's law, refusing only what compromises it. title: Fearful Times?
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Courage in Fearful Times
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen preaches from 2 Timothy 1:7 - “God has not given us the spirit of fear, but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind” - alongside Paul's charge to Timothy to share in the gospel's afflictions. He reads at length from Richard Wurmbrand's “Tortured for Christ,” recounting the author's conversion from atheism, the communist congress where clergy hailed Stalin, brainwashing answered by “heart washing,” and the maxim that the language of love and the language of seduction are the same. title: Sad Story Of Sattler
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The Legacy of Michael Sattler: Love and Law in the Anabaptist Movement
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen opens at 1 Timothy 1:5 and Romans 10:4, arguing that “the end of the commandment is charity” and “Christ is the end of the law” mean goal or target, not abolition. He then narrates the life of Michael Sattler from John Yoder's “The Legacy of Michael Sattler” - a Benedictine monk who joined the Anabaptists in 1525, chaired the 1527 Schleitheim Confession, and was tortured and burned weeks later. Tracing Sattler's letter to Capito and Bucer and the seven articles on baptism, the ban, the sword, and the oath, Bullen contends Sattler misread “love is the end of the law,” drifting into Marcionism, pacifism, and anti-government isolationism. title: Conspiracy In History
speaker: Jesse Herr
title_alt: Trusting Authority: Lessons from History
summary: In this sermon, Jesse Herr traces the human tendency, rooted in Genesis 3, to resent authority and assume those over us are “withholding good,” then to invent faults to justify disobedience. He surveys cases where a conspiracy charge was false - Korah against Moses in Numbers 16, the men of Abel and Joab in 2 Samuel 20, and Hanun's princes misreading David's kindness in 2 Samuel 10 - and cases of real betrayal, chiefly Saul's pursuit of David, where David still spares “the Lord's anointed” and mourns Saul's death. title: The Agency For Man - 2
speaker: Philip Herr
title_alt: Restoring the Candlestick: The Church's Role in Purging Sin
summary: In this study, Philip Herr builds on part one, starting in Revelation 1-2 where Christ walks among seven candlesticks and warns Ephesus that he will “remove thy candlestick.” He asks what practically changes when a church loses its candlestick. title: The Agency For Man
speaker: Philip Herr
title_alt: Restoration Through the Church: God's Agency for Humanity

From 2 Samuel 14:14 he shows that God “devises means” to bring back the banished, but only as changed men who will not damage the kingdom as Absalom did. title: What In The World Is Happening?
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Understanding the Parable of the Sower
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen expounds the parable of the sower from Luke 8:4-15, with parallels in Matthew 13, as God's own simple answer to what is really happening on earth. The seed is the word of God and is never at fault; the soil is the heart's condition toward God. title: The Balanced Mind
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Finding True Balance in Life
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen opens in Acts 24 and Acts 26, where Felix trembles, Festus calls Paul mad, and Agrippa is “almost persuaded,” yet all agree that Paul's call to “righteousness, temperance, and judgment to come” is unbalanced. Bullen redefines balance through a just weight, a balanced diet, a balanced tire, and an honest checkbook - everything working toward one goal with nothing opposing itself. From 2 Timothy 2:25 he shows God “instructing those that oppose themselves,” and from Romans 1:18-32 and John 3:20 that men “hold the truth in unrighteousness,” knowing better but fighting themselves. title: Samaritan - Good Or Bad
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: The True Meaning of Neighborly Love
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen asks whether the Samaritan of Luke 10 was good or bad, using the parable to expose how people misjudge by label rather than by conduct. The priest and Levite had the right pedigree and the wrong heart; the despised Samaritan “had compassion” and paid the cost. From 2 Kings 17 he reviews how the Samaritans came to “fear the LORD, and served their own gods,” and from John 4 how Jesus told the woman “ye worship ye know not what.” Yet a Samaritan leper returned to give thanks when nine Jews did not (Luke 17). title: What Think Ye Of Christ? - Part 2
speaker: Nathan Bullen
title_alt: Choosing Between Two Kingdoms: The True Cost of Discipleship
summary: In this sermon, Nathan Bullen continues “What think ye of Christ?” by turning from who Jesus is to who we are now. Building on Galatians 2:20 and Romans 6, he insists the “old man” and “body of sin” must be genuinely crucified, not merely malnourished - when a sin reappears, “go back and break their legs.” He frames the choice as Jesus or Barabbas, two belief systems both bearing the name Jesus, and reads Colossians 3's call to set affections above and put off wrath, malice, and lying.
