title: What Think Ye Of Christ?
speaker: Nathan Bullen
title_alt: Understanding the True Identity of Jesus
summary: In this sermon, Nathan Bullen asks Jesus' own question from Matthew 22:42, “What think ye of Christ?” He argues that familiarity with the name of Jesus keeps people from knowing Him, and that Scripture identifies Christ with the Word - “in the beginning was the Word, and the Word was God” (John 1). Working through 1 John 3 and John 14's “I am in the Father, and the Father in me,” he presses the point that a person is defined by what he does, not by his flesh, so that abiding in Christ means operating on the Father's standard. title: Unnecessary Pain
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Navigating Pain: Embracing God's Path to Healing
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen contrasts Genesis 1 and Revelation 21 - two worlds without pain - and distinguishes “necessary pain” from “unnecessary pain.” Necessary pain flows from the fall and from living on cursed ground; God gives His law, the family, and the church to carry believers through it, and it “worketh for us a far more exceeding weight of glory.” Unnecessary pain is self-inflicted through sin - the wasted 40 years after the twelve spies, the works of the flesh in Romans 1 and Galatians 5:19-21, the warnings of 1 Corinthians 6:9-10. title: The Name Of God Is Blasphemed
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Representing God: The Responsibility of Christians
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen expounds Romans 2:17-24, where Paul tells the professing Jew that “the name of God is blasphemed among the Gentiles through you.” He applies it to Christians, citing 1 Timothy 6:1, Titus 2:5-10, and 2 Peter 2:1-3, where false teachers “privately shall bring in damnable heresies” so that “the way of truth shall be evil spoken of.” Bullen argues that believers who misrepresent God hand the world ammunition, but that slander is not always the church's fault. title: "...And The Rains Came Tumbling Down..."
speaker: Mark Bullen
title_alt: Building on the Rock: Foundations of Faith
summary: In this sermon, Mark Bullen opens in Deuteronomy 6, where Moses commands parents to teach God's words “diligently unto thy children,” and pairs it with Jesus' wise and foolish builders in Luke 6:46-49. Drawing on his own contracting experience, he argues that a life must be dug down and connected to bedrock - Christ and the law of God - or the floods will undermine it and shift it out of shape. He holds up Phinehas, son of Eleazar (Numbers 25), as a preacher's kid who stayed “zealous for his God” across generations, contrasted with Eli's sons Hophni and Phinehas, who disgraced their name. title: Why I Live In Linn County
speaker: Jesse Herr
title_alt: Living by God's Instructions: A Journey of Faith
summary: In this sermon, Jesse Herr explains “why I live in Linn County,” marking fifteen years since he moved there as a single man to join Living Faith Christian Fellowship. From Matthew 7:28-29 he notes that Jesus “taught as one having authority,” perfectly in line with Scripture, and from Ephesians 2:19-22 that the church is “built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets.” He reads from an old notebook the church checklist and life goals he wrote while seeking God, and describes how stepping out in faith - even over growing a beard - brought eternity “powerfully impressed on my mind.” His conversion at eighteen turned on seeing that God “is more interested in my well-being than I am,” an

title: Refreshing Our Vision
speaker: Jesse Herr
title_alt: The Power of Unity in the Church
summary: In this sermon, Jesse Herr calls the church to refresh its vision of what God intends for His body. From Matthew 18 he notes that “thy brother is in church with you,” and from Hebrews 10 that assembling exists to warn against willful sin, not to promote eternal security. Jesus prays in John 17 “that they all may be one... that the world may believe,” so unity carries a convicting power the devil works to destroy. Ephesians 4 sets the goal: growing “unto a perfect man, unto the measure of the stature of the fullness of Christ.” He urges esteeming leaders who “watch for your souls” and “must give account,” warns from Exodus 17 that those who straggle alone are exposed like the ones Amalek stru
